1598.inspectionNotes: Sense → Think → Act block diagram: camera/lidar/IMU, CPU/GPU/MCU, motors/servos. Definition is a physical machine sensing, processing and acting. No printed footer number is visible on this page; physical page retained separately. The statement that compute runs AI is a course focus, not a claim that every robot requires machine learning.

1599.inspectionNotes: Six hardware subsystem boxes: structural links/joints/chassis, battery/PSU/wiring, motors/servos/pneumatics, cameras/lidars/encoders, MCU/SBC/GPU, and ROS/CAN/Wi-Fi communications. ROS software middleware and bus/network technologies are different abstraction levels. Footer 5.

1600.inspectionNotes: Full six-row materials table inspected: steel 5 stars/heavy/low cost/industrial welding; aluminum 4 stars/light/medium/cobots and drones; CFRP 5 stars/very light/high/medical and aerospace; titanium 5 stars/medium/very high/surgical; engineering plastics 2 stars/very light/very low/education; soft silicone flexible/light/medium/soft grippers and wearables. Qualitative class-level tradeoffs, not universal grade-specific strength rankings. Lighter links reduce inertia under comparable geometry, but faster tracking and easier learning are not unconditional guarantees.

1601.inspectionNotes: Hydraulic and pneumatic descriptions plus both cutaway cylinders viewed. Hydraulic upper image has rod extending left, right-port inward arrow and left-port outward arrow; pneumatic lower image has rod right, left-port inward blue arrow and right-port outward green arrow. Hydraulic high force and actuator-level power density are balanced against peripheral pump/plumbing mass, leaks and seal friction. Air compressibility and seal friction complicate pneumatic control. Cleaner refers to working-fluid leakage, not a guarantee of zero exhaust contamination.

1602.inspectionNotes: Brushed DC text: stationary brushes contact revolving commutator to energize rotor windings; torque proportional to winding current in the stated model; winding overheating limits sustained operation. Electric motors are controllable and easy to interface. The unlabelled cutaway is generic motor imagery and is not proof of a visible brushed commutator. Relative fluid-versus-electric power density depends on the comparison boundary.

1603.inspectionNotes: Brushless: stationary windings and rotating magnetic rotor, electronic commutation from shaft position, reduced brush wear and favorable cooling. Internal shaft sensor is an example, not mandatory because sensorless commutation exists. Claims of infrequent AC motors and low-torque steppers need historical/task qualification, not current blanket truth. Better cooling and torque are design-dependent.

1604.inspectionNotes: Five gripper boxes inspected: two-finger parallel for boxes/warehouse; three-finger adaptive for irregular shapes; vacuum for flat packages/glass; inflatable silicone soft fingers for delicate food/medical; magnetic for metal sheets/castings. Magnetic attraction needs suitable material, not all metals. Vacuum needs an appropriate seal/surface and payload margin. End-effector is terminal tool/device, not necessarily the structural last link itself. Simpler action space can ease learning but does not guarantee task success.

1605.inspectionNotes: Two-column sensor classification: source places encoders, IMU, current sensors and force/torque under proprioception; RGB, depth/LiDAR, ultrasonic and tactile arrays under exteroception. F/T contact measurements can describe external interaction, so classification is context-dependent; preserve source table without asserting a universal placement. Current is a torque estimate via a motor model, not direct contact wrench. Tactile arrays give spatial contact distribution.

1606.inspectionNotes: Full sensor-output-use-rate table: encoder counts/joint RL state/1–10 kHz; RGB-D image plus depth/grasp pose/30–90 fps; LiDAR point cloud/SLAM and avoidance/10–20 Hz; IMU acceleration and gyro/stabilization and balance/100–1000 Hz. These are illustrative ranges, not specifications for every sensor. LiDAR may be planar as explicitly recognized later; not every device yields native 3-D scans.

1607.inspectionNotes: Compute examples and all values read: MCU Arduino/STM32 8–240 MHz, kB RAM, under 1 W, PID/rules/reading; Pi 4 SBC 1.8 GHz quad-core, 4 GB, 5 W, OpenCV/light ML; Jetson Nano 128 CUDA cores plus ARM, 4 GB, 5–10 W, YOLOv8/policy inference. These are example configurations, not class-wide maxima or workload guarantees. PID is classical control, not inherently ML. Real-time feasibility needs measured latency, model and precision details.

1608.inspectionNotes: AGX Orin source example 2048 CUDA cores, 64 GB, 275 TOPS, 15–60 W; FPGA Zynq parallel hardware logic, deterministic, 5–20 W; cloud/5G offload for LLM planning/heavy training. TOPS and power depend on configuration and precision; deterministic FPGA timing requires design. Cloud GPUs are not unlimited, and network latency/jitter/outage remain. Hardware resource abundance is not end-to-end deadline proof.

1609.inspectionNotes: Full battery table inspected: Li-Po 150–250 Wh/kg, up to 100C, 300–500 cycles, drones/racing; Li-ion 18650 100–200 Wh/kg, 1–3C, 500–1000 cycles, mobile/humanoids; NiMH 60–120 Wh/kg, 5–10C, 500 cycles, older education; lead-acid 30–50 Wh/kg, low discharge, 200–300 cycles, heavy AGVs. Values are broad illustrative entries, not battery-selection limits. Li-Po is a lithium-ion family/package distinction and 18650 is a cylindrical form factor, not the full chemistry. All-hardware-electrical wording omits hydraulic/pneumatic mechanical power paths. BMS is in heading only, with no actual functional block diagram.

1610.inspectionNotes: Power example fully read: two drive motors at 5 W each, Jetson Nano 10 W, sensors 5 W gives 25 W. Battery 2.5 Ah at 11.1 V gives nominal 27.75 Wh and ideal 1.11 h = 66.6 min; source approximately 66 min is a coarse approximation, not a key arithmetic conflict. Usable capacity, losses, changing voltage/load and reserve reduce practical runtime. No wiring schematic or BMS behavior is supplied.

1611.inspectionNotes: UART/serial source range 115 kbps–10 Mbps with MCU/GPS/debugging/RPLiDAR examples; I²C expanded Inter-Integrated Circuit, 100 kbps–1 Mbps with MPU6050/ToF/OLED; CAN 1 Mbps for joints and automotive ECUs. Listed speeds are illustrative, not limits of every UART, I²C mode or CAN variant. Payload throughput differs from bit rate because framing/arbitration overhead exists.

1612.inspectionNotes: EtherCAT source 100 Mbps and deterministic for real-time cobot motor control; ROS 2/DDS shown over Wi-Fi, network-dependent for sensor/planner/driver nodes. ROS 2/DDS is middleware rather than a Wi-Fi-only physical protocol; no network-dependent rate alone guarantees hard-real-time latency. Timing and QoS/design still matter.

1613.inspectionNotes: All six hardware-to-AI rows inspected. State q=[0.3,−0.1,1.2] rad; action PWM 75% claimed to yield 75% speed; reward +10 for stable grasp force; policy inference 8 ms; encoder ±0.088° claimed to map to Gaussian sigma=0.001 rad; RL step 100 Hz claimed to require IMU at least 200 Hz. Qualifications: observation need not equal full state, reward is designed from measured conditions, duty is not a universal speed percentage, a quantization bound does not determine Gaussian distribution/sigma, and Nyquist concerns signal bandwidth rather than twice a policy update rate. Better sensors can help, but performance also depends on calibration, timing, compute and algorithms.

1614.inspectionNotes: Manipulator fusion motivations: redundancy, accuracy, robustness, completeness. Sensors: encoders/resolvers joint angles/velocities; F/T end-effector six-component wrench; IMUs vibration/orientation estimates; RGB-D/stereo object and pose; tactile/skin contact distribution/slip. Methods list Kalman, EKF, particle, deep CNN/LSTM fusion and Bayesian estimation. A wrench has three force and three moment components, not six independently actuated DOFs. Fusion improvements require error models, calibration, synchronization, correlation handling and fault detection, not blind averaging.

1615.inspectionNotes: Mobile palette: planar/3-D LiDAR, wheel-odometry dead reckoning, IMU, outdoor GNSS, stereo/RGB-D, near-range ultrasound/IR. Right-hand five-stage SLAM pipeline: raw LiDAR/odometry/IMU; filtering/calibration/sync; point clouds/keypoints/edges; EKF or graph-SLAM state estimation/loop closure; map and pose for planning. Not all LiDAR has 360-degree field of view. Loop closure and global consistency are algorithm/data-association goals, not guaranteed by any sensor list or EKF name.

1616.inspectionNotes: Summary includes new structural point: links/joints determine DOF and workspace; calls six-DOF articulated arms most flexible. Qualify task-dependent dexterity, reachable set and singularities; six joints do not guarantee every pose. Servo angle state and PWM action, gripper action space, force feedback for compliance, observation quality repeat previous content. Bottom text approaches footer but remains readable.

1617.inspectionNotes: Final summary: low-level MCU versus Jetson/GPU inference, power-runtime, latency-RL step frequency; hardware/state/action/reward mapping and sensor fusion. Sim-to-real gap attributed to hardware imperfections, but simulation/model/environment/task mismatch also contributes; not exclusively defective hardware. Reward remains a software objective using hardware evidence.

qualifications: Author judgments and checks are not independent review; all source formulas explained in numerical questions carry symbol/unit/assumption metadata.
